paper.title_en: Geometric properties of concatenated geometric and holonomic quantum gates
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the geometric properties of concatenated quantum gates, focusing on the distinction between geometric and holonomic quantum computation. We show that, although individual gates may be purely geometric, their concatenation does not generally preserve this property, since the cyclic states of the composite operation can accumulate nontrivial dynamical phases over the course of the concatenated evolution. In contrast, we demonstrate that concatenations of arbitrary single-qubit holonomic gates remain holonomic, provided that the parallel-transport condition holds throughout the evolution and the computational subspace undergoes cyclic evolution. The preservation of geometric or holonomic character under concatenation is an important prerequisite for extending arguments underlying geometric protection from individual gates to complete quantum circuits.
